newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends firm as China buys, soymeal mixed.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends firm as China buys, soymeal mixed.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed firmer on Tuesday, boosted by confirmation China bought U.S. soyoil, but soymeal values were mixed on bear spreading.

Export sources said China bought 35,000 tonnes U.S. soyoil on Monday. Traders noted rumors had been in the market last week as commercials were heavy buyers of soyoil but confirmation of the business lent support, they said.

China also bought at least 16,000 tonnes Argentine and Brazilian soyoil on Monday. The purchases provided some optimism that China would remain an active player despite reports buyers had filled nearby needs.
Nearby soymeal futures ended weaker, pressured by bear spreading.
Traders said Rosenthal Collins spread 200 lots July/March and 100 lots May/March. FIMAT Futures spread 100 lots July/March.
Scattered rains continued to fall in Brazil's key soybean growing regions but growers in Parana said their crops might suffer if heavy rains continued much longer.
Soyoil ended 0.06 to 0.10 cent per lb higher with March up 0.06 at 23.86 cents. Soymeal closed $0.70 per ton higher to $0.60 lower with March down $0.60 at $235.60.
On the day, ADM sold 200 lots May soymeal and Cargill Inc sold 300 August and 100 each March and May, traders said, and Rosenthal Collins bought and sold 300 March.
In soyoil, ABN-Chicago Corporation bought 250 lots March and 50 May, traders said. R.J. O'Brien sold 500 lots March.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 14,000 contracts, below the 14,719 traded Monday.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, slightly above the 11,854 traded Monday.
